text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm proposing a change to the admission curve for west-2 tonight. moving away from immediate hard rejects during brief saturation to a staged softfail + short queuing window. goal: keep p99 latency under 300ms while lowering token cost for bursts.

sam: can you sketch the high-level tradeoffs? why not just increase queue depth?

maya: queue depth helps throughput but spikes hurt latency and memory. softfail lets us serve degraded responses (smaller model or truncated tokens) for a short window, then reject if still saturated. reduces cold-starts and token churn.

jordan: thinking in terms of burst credits: allow short bursts up to X tokens per customer, then switch to degrade for Y seconds, then hard reject. keeps fairness and avoids long tail queues.

elena: important: what about Dedicated customers with SLAs? we can't silently degrade their traffic. need opt-out/whitelist. also need clear audit logs for any degraded responses.

maya: yep — whitelist key for reserved capacity + explicit policy: dedicated=true => bypass degrade and go to quota-based reject only. we'll log degraded=true and model_variant in the trace.

nick: network/egress cost angle: some degradation paths swap to a smaller model hosted in a remote region — that could increase egress and cross-region latency. prefer local smaller-quantized variant when possible.

jordan: agree. prefer local quantized variant first, then remote fallback. also propose a cost-lookup table used by the router: prefer option with lowest estimated cost within latency budget.

ops-bot: plan-created maya:1769312468 policy-change/softfail-west-2 canary=10pct window=2h monitor=[p99_latency,serve_rate,queue_depth,token_cost_per_min]

maya: sample policy snippet (pseudo config):
```yaml
admission_policy:
  mode: staged_softfail
  burst_tokens: 1500
  degrade_window_seconds: 10
  degrade_action: 
    - prefer_local_variant: true
    - truncate_tokens_to: 512
  hard_reject_after_seconds: 30
  whitelist: ["dedicated-*", "enterprise-*"]
  metrics: ["p99_latency","queue_depth","degraded_rate","token_cost_minute"]
```

sam: what observability do we need to feel confident?

maya: dashboards for per-region p99, per-customer degraded_rate, cost delta vs baseline, and an alert if degraded_rate > 20% for > 5min. also spike alert on queue_depth > 50 for any node group.

leo: runbook note: if degraded_rate triggers, rollback policy, scale up warm-pool by +20% (if capacity available), and open a pager if Dedicated customers affected.

elena: add a compliance check: for any request with degraded=true we must persist original prompt hash + variant used for 30 days for eval/regression.

jordan: experiment idea: compare two degrade strategies in canary A/B — A: token truncation to 512 + quantized small variant; B: immediate switch to smaller variant w/ full tokens. measure user-level quality regressions via eval set and p99 latency improvements.

nick: quick numbers we should simulate: cost delta assuming 10k rps burst sustained 30s in west-2, local quantized variant saves ~45% cost, remote fallback costs +30% egress. will run sim later.

maya: rollout plan: 1) deploy policy to staging + run soak 24h; 2) enable canary 10% west-2 for 2h with heavy synthetic bursts; 3) if metrics green, expand to 50% with 6h window; 4) full roll. rollback if p99 or degraded_rate breaches thresholds.

sam: LGTM. please post the experiment sim results and the exact rollback thresholds before 18:00 PST.

maya: will do. tagging @ops-bot to create the canary job and @leo for runbook updates. :thumbsup:
